title: Nailfold capillaroscopy
what: Using a special microscope, the doctor looks at the tiny blood vessels at the edge of your fingernails.
why: When your fingers turn pale or blue in the cold, and when certain connective tissue diseases are suspected.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; the report is ready right away or within a day
tell_doctor: If your fingers change color in the cold
If you have injuries or damaged skin near your nails

prepare.title: Nails
prepare.text: For about a week before, do not get a manicure or cut your cuticles. Remove nail polish.

prepare.title: Before the test
prepare.text: On the day of the test, it is better not to smoke or drink coffee. Check with the clinic.

prepare.title: Warmth
prepare.text: Come early so your hands can warm up in the room.

bring: Results of past tests, if any
steps: You sit down and rest your hand on a table
Your hands get used to the warm room for a few minutes
A drop of oil is put on the skin near the nail
The doctor looks at each finger under the microscope
Pictures are saved for the report
feel: You need to keep your hand calm and still
after: The oil is wiped off, and you can go
The report is given right away or within a day
Go over the result with the doctor who referred you

faq.a: It damages the skin near the nail, and the capillaries are hard to see.
No. It is just a look under magnification.

reminders.text: Capillaroscopy tomorrow. Remove your nail polish. Do not smoke or drink coffee in the morning.
